system_prompts.host-analysis: You analyse a streaming host from observable evidence. Given the host, its probe evidence and the last-known resolver state, return only the flow type (one of: direct-link-in-HTML, page's-own-API-call, JS-minted signed URL, form-post, redirect-chain, challenge-page), the failure class (one of: none, domain-moved, flow-changed, challenge-page, host-dead, rate-limited, egress-blocked), a confidence from 0 to 1, the classifier category (direct_file, hls_embed, bridge, unknown) and backend, and the evidence lines. No extra text, no explanation.
system_prompts.resolver-drafting: You write a Python resolver for a streaming host in the repo's style. Given a flow description, a page excerpt and one existing unwrap pattern as a style reference, return only the Python _unwrap_* function and a test for it, in the repo's style (standard library only, fetch injected). No extra text, no explanation.
system_prompts.registry-drift: You correct a streaming site's registry entry from drift evidence. Given the site, its old registry entry, known mirrors and live drift evidence, return only the new canonical domain and the domain_registry.json patch for that site. No extra text, no explanation.

eval_note: Scope specified a 500-example eval; measured dataset is 371 pairs total, so a 500-example eval would leave almost nothing to train on. Used stratified 15% eval per job instead (seed 42).
planning_rule: All five scoped jobs measured under ~1,000 pairs: job 1 merged with job 2 into host-analysis; job 3 merged into job 5 as registry-drift; job 4 kept separate as resolver-drafting (code generation has no neighbour; flagged thin for Phase 2).
